correctness.rationale: Direct Bernoulli product gives mean pq^{d_v}; joint isolation is zero on an edge and p²q^{d_u+d_v−c_uv} otherwise, so covariance sign exactly recovers adjacency. A positive pair gives q^{-c_uv}; absence of distance-two pairs forces clique components. Distinct component orders give q by ratios of means; equal K_k components have identical full law at exactly the two roots of p(1−p)^{k−1}, except unique critical p=1/k. Repeated nonedge co-isolation and union bound give stated exponential failure bound without knowing p. Independent exact graph checks n≤4 verified 410 pair instances.

value.rationale: Recovering a labelled graph from isolation-only observations and characterizing precisely when unknown site-retention p is not identifiable are natural inverse-probability problems. The complete all-host classification and constructive finite-sample guarantee are useful exact statements, not merely a tiny illustrative instance.

final_claim: For every finite labelled graph and uniform independent site-retention p∈(0,1), isolation-indicator covariance determines the graph; the exact exceptional twofold p ambiguity occurs only for unions of equal-size K_k with k≥2 away from p=1/k, and a finite-sample graph decoder has the stated bound.
limitations: Requires aligned labels, independent identical site retention, exact moments; the decoder bound is sufficient not optimal.
